LESSON: READING 5.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION – PLAYS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you read for information?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary related to cultural heritage for language acquisition
2. respond to a text on the theme for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 5.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION – PLAYS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 5.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION – PLAYS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary related to cultural heritage for language acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary related to cultural heritage for language acquisition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary related to cultural heritage for language acquisition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary related to cultural heritage for language acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to a text on the theme for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to a text on the theme for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to a text on the theme for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to a text on the theme for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary related to cultural heritage for language acquisition)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays to a partner. (skill: respond to a text on the theme for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary related to cultural heritage for language acquisition.
3. Practise this skill: respond to a text on the theme for comprehension.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you read for information?
2. How can plays be used to preserve our cultural heritage?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary related to cultural heritage for language acquisition.
5. Be able to: respond to a text on the theme for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
